metadata.title: DOM-based XSS via document.write() in Print Functionality — Session Hijacking

sources: ApplinX REST API GetScreenResponse fields[].content (server-controlled terminal data)
transformations: generateObjectArray() copies field.content to obj['data'] — no encoding
formatLineText() / GXUtils.replaceString() — plain string operations, no HTML encoding
sinks: document.getElementById('copyDiv').innerHTML = this.copyData — FALSE POSITIVE (innerText assignment path HTML-encodes content)

privilege_boundary.achieved_privilege: Authenticated browser session — gx_token, sessionStorage, same-origin REST API calls

impact.description: Session token (gx_token / Bearer auth) stolen. Attacker can impersonate user for all ApplinX REST API calls: read terminal screens, send keystrokes, access/delete macros. Integrity: attacker can send keystrokes to mainframe applications. Root of attack chains AC-001 and AC-003.

prerequisites: ApplinX REST API backend compromised OR MITM on unencrypted REST channel
Authenticated user must click Print button (user interaction required)
No CSP blocking inline event handlers

remediation.fix_approach:
Replace document.write('
' + element + '
') with createElement('div') + textContent = element. Alternatively use already-injected DomSanitizer. Add Content-Security-Policy: script-src 'self'.

history.note: R-M-003: document.write() with unsanitized server screen content + modalpopup innerHTML = this.copyData bypass Angular sanitization

Confirmed XSS in formatPrintPage() document.write() sink. Copy modal innerHTML is FALSE POSITIVE (innerText path HTML-encodes). Scanner CVSS refined: HIGH 7.6 (AC:H requires backend compromise; PR:H). Root of AC-001 (token theft) and AC-003 (sessionStorage → path traversal chain).
